title: JPMorgan says cyberattack on third-party vendors may have exposed some customer data
date_note: Published November 19; date of the vendor attack not stated.
summary: JPMorgan said on Thursday 19 November that third-party service providers were attacked and it believes attackers accessed certain marketing data held by them, which may include some customer names and email addresses. It reported no disruption to its services and would contact affected customers, offering complimentary credit monitoring where appropriate. Reuters says leaked data it reviewed appears to include 124 bank employee and more than 16,000 customer email addresses, which it could not verify.
plain: JPMorgan says outside companies it uses were hacked and some customers' names and email addresses may have been exposed; it says it will contact those affected.
exec: Vendor-held customer contact data is a phishing risk and shows how third-party suppliers extend a bank's exposure.
action: General advice: JPMorgan customers should be wary of unexpected emails that mention their account; JPMorgan says it will contact affected customers directly.
impact: Some customer names and email addresses may be exposed. Reuters says leaked data it reviewed appears to include 124 bank employee and more than 16,000 customer email addresses, which it could not verify. Newsweek separately relates data published by a group called n0n to Visa's Reserve card program.
